text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak told an international press conference: Israel wants us to pressure (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat to accept its proposals, and this will never happen. Egypt does not think of cutting relations (with Israel) and Israel will be the loser if it pushes us into such a situation.
- Israeli Prime Minister's political adviser, Dore Gold, arrived into Egypt on Wednesday for talks with senior foreign ministry officials.
- Mubarak underlined, at a meeting with members of Egyptian Labourers Federation, the government's concern about the social dimension of Egypt's economic reforms.
- The cabinet decides to forgive all loans due on residents of the Suez Canal and north Sinai area since 1974. The finance ministry will pay out all loans.
- Egypt is negotiating 12 projects worth $7 billion with Egyptian, Arab and foreign partners. The projects were presented during the Cairo economic conference.
- The Public Attorney, Ragaa el-Arabi, banned four National Cement officials from travelling out of the country. They are accused of illegally taking 436 million pounds from the state's funds.
- Egypt's local debt reached 156 billion pounds by the end of June, Finance Minister Mohieddin El-Gharib said.
